hook: You lose entire evenings to your phone and wake up vaguely ashamed. And then you do it again.
topic: Default Behaviour / Environment and the Soft Life Audit
body:
**You know exactly how it goes. The phone comes out for five minutes. Two hours later, you're still there.**

You wake up the next morning with that low feeling. Not quite guilt. Just — you know you didn't spend that time the way you would have chosen to.

And then you do it again.

This is not a willpower failure. This is an environment that is set up to produce exactly the outcome you are getting. The phone is there. The friction to use it is zero. The friction to do something else is higher. So the phone wins, every time, regardless of your intentions.

A disciplined man does not out-willpower a bad environment daily. That is not a sustainable strategy and it never has been.

He changes the environment so the right behaviour is easier than the wrong one.

Phone in another room at 9pm. Charger in the kitchen. The book on the table where the phone used to be.

This is not a philosophy. It is a configuration problem. And configuration problems have configuration solutions.
visual_direction: Marcus still, unhurried. Long pause after "And then you do it again." Let the viewer sit in the recognition. Text overlay appears during the reframe.
